depth.summary: A heavily traded stock and a barely traded one can both show tight spreads, so the spread alone can mislead you about liquidity. A big market order can fill at several prices when one price does not hold enough shares. The number of shares showing at the best bid or ask is usually small. Liquidity means there are buyers and sellers ready to trade with your order, competing on price.
